title: Cold Storage Building in Pakistan: Steel Frame Guide | Steel Mind Engineers
description: What a steel frame must do for a cold store in Pakistan: panel supports, sealed joints, equipment loads, floors and doors. Plan your cold storage building.
h1: Cold Storage Buildings in Pakistan: What the Steel Frame Must Do
quickAnswer: A cold store keeps goods at a set temperature, so the building must stop heat from entering. The steel frame carries the insulated roof and wall panels, the refrigeration equipment and the doors. Plan sealed joints, a tight envelope and the equipment loads from the first drawing, and coordinate with your cooling specialist.
alt: Cold storage steel building in Pakistan

faq.q: Can the steel frame carry refrigeration units?
faq.a: Yes. The engineer designs the frame for these loads.

faq.q: What temperature range can the store hold?
faq.a: That depends on the panels and the cooling system. Tell the engineer your target temperature.

faq.q: Does Steel Mind Engineers install the refrigeration plant?
faq.a: No. The cooling specialist you choose installs it, and Steel Mind Engineers coordinates the loads and openings.

blocks.text: A cold store keeps goods at a set temperature, whether for fruit, vegetables, dairy, meat or medicines. In Pakistan's heat, every gap in the building lets warm air in, and the cooling system works harder and costs more to run. A cold storage building in Pakistan therefore needs a tight envelope: thick insulated panels, sealed joints, well-fitted doors and a floor that does not carry heat from the ground. The steel frame is the skeleton behind all of this, and it must be designed with the cold store in mind and not as an ordinary shed.

In a steel cold store building, the frame holds up everything else. It carries the roof and wall panels, the doors, the lights and the heavy refrigeration equipment. It also provides the structure for the loading area and canopy. The frame must be strong enough for these loads and accurate enough that panels fit tightly. Steel Mind Engineers supplies the steel frame, the roof and wall structure and the supports for insulated panels, and coordinates the loads and openings with the cooling specialist you choose.

Insulated panel warehouse walls and roofs use panels with an insulating core. Thicker panels reduce heat gain, and sealed joints keep warm air and moisture out. The panel supports must be straight and accurately placed, because gaps appear where the supports are uneven. The target temperature decides the panel thickness, so tell the engineer how cold the store must be. A store for chilled goods needs a different panel from a store for frozen goods.

blocks.title: Avoiding Heat Paths in the Steel

blocks.text: Steel conducts heat well. If a steel member runs from outside to inside without a break, it carries heat into the cold room. Frame connections are detailed to avoid such heat paths where possible, and panels are fixed so that the steel stays outside the insulated envelope where the design allows. Good detailing at the base, at the eaves and around openings helps the refrigeration system run efficiently. This is one reason to speak to the steel engineer before the panels are ordered.

Condensers, ducts, pipes and evaporators are heavy, and they hang from or stand on the roof and the frames. The roof and frames must carry these loads without sagging. The refrigeration plant is installed by the specialist you choose, and Steel Mind Engineers coordinates the loads and the openings with that specialist. Share the equipment drawings early. A change in equipment late in the project can mean strengthening the frame.

The floor of a cold store needs insulation, because cold flows into the ground. Doors must seal tightly and open quickly, since each opening lets warm air in. Insulated sectional doors and PU-filled doors suit cold rooms. Vapor barriers and good detailing prevent water from forming inside the walls, which damages insulation and steel. Ask your cooling specialist to review the details of the floor and the doors.

A cold store needs a covered loading area, so goods do not warm up while waiting for the truck. A dock with a steel canopy and tight-sealing doors keeps the cold chain intact. Plan the dock height, the door count and the yard depth together. See the Warehouses with Loading Docks page for details. Fast loading matters even more for cold goods than for dry goods.

blocks.title: Who Uses Cold Storage and Why Steel Suits It

blocks.text: Fruit and vegetable traders, dairy and meat processors, pharmaceutical distributors and food exporters use cold stores. Steel suits them because it is quick to build, which helps before a harvest or an export season, and because bolted frames allow extension when volumes grow. A steel frame also gives wide clear spans, which leave room for racks and handling equipment.
